correctness.rationale: For q=2^f, the twisted dual-number ring with Frobenius twist has unit group K^+ semidirect K^×, with conjugation by a acting as multiplication by a^{-1}; inversion of the cyclic complement identifies this with AGL_1(K). For odd q>3, trivial center forces any finite realizing ring to have characteristic two. Its Jacobson subgroup 1+J is a normal 2-subgroup, while AGL_1(q) has none because any such subgroup centralizes the odd translation kernel and the latter is self-centralizing. Thus the ring is semisimple. Trivial center forces every nontrivial Artin--Wedderburn field factor to be F_2. Direct indecomposability leaves one GL_n(F_2), and simplicity for n>=3 reduces to GL_2(F_2)=S_3, forcing q=3. The packaged checker verifies the complete explicit positive construction for q=2,4,8,16.

originality.rationale: Lockridge--Terkel's 2024 paper studies degree-one affine groups only over Z/nZ, where the additive group is cyclic; its full text merely notes AGL_1(F_4)=A_4 as an example showing the finite-field situation differs from the holomorph case. The older twisted-dual-number paper gives the semidirect-product unit group that supplies the even-field construction but does not formulate a Fuchs realizability classification. Davis--Occhipinti cover A_4 as an isolated alternating-group case. Targeted semantic and web searches found no classification of AGL_1(F_q) as finite-ring unit groups for arbitrary q.
residual_risks: The positive even-field construction is implicit in the known unit group of twisted dual numbers.

The proof uses standard finite-ring and finite-simple-group structure, so novelty lies in the complete classification and its uniform construction rather than in the individual ingredients.

value.rationale: The primary 2024 paper makes affine linear groups a central test family for Fuchs' problem but classifies degree one only when the additive group is cyclic. Finite fields are the most natural omitted coefficient rings, and the answer exhibits a sharp structural dichotomy: every even field works through one uniform local construction, whereas all odd fields except F_3 are obstructed. This simultaneously explains the known A_4 example, produces infinite new realizable affine groups such as AGL_1(F_8), and closes the degree-one finite-field case.
